name: Gottman-informed couples therapy
heroTitle: Understand the friendship. Change the conversation.
summary: Explore the relationship foundations, conflict practices, and shared meaning emphasized in Gottman-informed work, with examples that distinguish a useful repair from pressure to move on.
panelTitle: A stronger relationship is more than fewer arguments.
panelParagraphs: The method considers everyday friendship and connection as well as how partners navigate disagreements. A technique should serve the relationship, not become a scorecard.
safety: Communication tools are not a treatment for coercion or a requirement to remain in an unsafe relationship. A clinician must assess safety and appropriateness before joint exercises, and harmful behavior remains the responsibility of the person doing it.

model.title: Conflict sits within a larger relationship.
paragraphs: The Gottman Method organizes work around a relationship framework that includes friendship, responding to bids for connection, managing conflict, and creating shared meaning. Trust and commitment are important parts of that framework. The emphasis is not only on what happens during an argument but also on the everyday relationship around it.

Gottman-informed therapy may draw on selected ideas or interventions from this approach. That description is different from confirming a particular certification level, a complete assessment package, or use of every part of the method. The actual plan should reflect the clinician's training and the couple's needs.

One useful distinction is between addressing a specific complaint and attacking a person's character. Another is between interrupting escalation and resolving the underlying disagreement. A calmer conversation can create room for the issue; it does not automatically settle it.

panel.title: Learn about each other, not a set of scores.
paragraphs: A framework can organize questions. It cannot decide whether your relationship is healthy, whether both people are safe, or what the future should be from a few online examples.

example.title: The dishes are the topic. Feeling alone is part of the experience.
example.intro: This fictional example concerns an ordinary household disagreement between partners who can speak safely.

items.title: The opening
paragraphs: Alex comes home to a kitchen full of dishes and says, You never help. Riley hears an accusation about their character and starts listing everything they did that day.

items.title: The escalation
paragraphs: The discussion moves away from the kitchen into a contest about who contributes more. Both people become focused on defending themselves instead of agreeing on what needs doing.

items.title: A possible repair
paragraphs: Alex notices the conversation is getting sharper and asks to restart with one specific concern. Riley is free to say they need a pause before returning to the issue.

reveal.title: What changes when the request becomes specific?
paragraphs: A restart could identify the concrete observation, describe its impact, and make a manageable request. It could also include recognition that work done elsewhere is real. This does not guarantee agreement about fairness, but it makes the subject easier to discuss than a global judgment about a partner.

The repair is only one piece. A lasting change might require an actual division-of-labor conversation and follow-through. Repeating apologies or softer wording without changing responsibilities would leave the substantive issue unresolved.

toolsTitle: Four areas that can make the method easier to understand.
toolsIntro: These are educational descriptions, not a complete Gottman assessment or an assigned couple exercise.

tools.title: Friendship and knowing each other
tools.teaser: Keep an interest in the person whose life is changing alongside yours.
paragraphs: Knowing a partner is not a one-time task completed early in a relationship. Interests, stressors, hopes, and responsibilities can change. Gottman-informed work may include attention to that ongoing knowledge rather than concentrating exclusively on problems.
Curiosity is different from surveillance. Privacy and personal boundaries still matter.

tools.title: Bids and everyday responses
tools.teaser: Notice the small invitations that can be easy to miss.
paragraphs: A bid for connection may be a question, a comment, an expression of interest, or a request for attention. The idea is to consider how ordinary responses contribute to connection, not to tally every missed cue as evidence of rejection.
A response can include a respectful limit and a later opportunity to connect.

tools.title: Conflict and repair
tools.teaser: Reduce destructive exchanges while keeping the actual issue in view.
paragraphs: The approach describes patterns such as criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and withdrawal during overwhelming interactions. The value of the terms is noticing a behavior that could change, not labeling a partner as the problem.
Repair attempts and pauses should support returning to a conversation safely. They do not require immediate forgiveness.

tools.title: Meaning, dreams and differences
tools.teaser: Understand what an issue represents before trying to solve it.
paragraphs: A disagreement can connect to personal values, family experiences, or hopes for the future. Some differences need ongoing management rather than a final winner. Learning what matters to each person can change the quality of the discussion.
Understanding why something matters is not the same as agreeing to it.

processTitle: Assessment, practice, and application belong together.

process.title: Understand the relationship
paragraphs: A clinician may ask about history, strengths, stressors, conflict, and individual perspectives. Confirm which assessment and individual-contact policies actually apply.

process.title: Choose the work
paragraphs: The plan might focus on friendship, a recurring conflict, rebuilding trust, or discussing shared meaning. A method should not require ignoring the concern that brought you in.

process.title: Try and reflect
paragraphs: Practice may happen during the session with therapist feedback. What is useful for one couple may need adaptation for another.

process.title: Review the daily difference
paragraphs: Look beyond whether an exercise went smoothly. Consider whether the couple communicates more clearly, follows through, and experiences meaningful change outside appointments.

limitsTitle: Research-informed does not mean one exercise fits everyone.

limits.title: No relationship verdict from a label
paragraphs: A webpage cannot predict divorce or score a relationship from a few examples. Named patterns are a language for exploring behavior, not an automated diagnosis or proof that a relationship is beyond repair.

limits.title: The clinician and service still matter
paragraphs: Gottman-informed describes an influence on the work. Ask about relevant training, the process offered, and how concerns about fit are handled. Do not infer certification from a method name on a profile.

questions.question: Will every disagreement be solved?
paragraphs: No method can promise that. Some disagreements concern lasting differences. A useful aim may be understanding and managing those differences without repeated injury, while identifying where actual decisions and commitments are needed.

questions.question: Do both partners have homework?
paragraphs: Some clinicians suggest between-session practice. Ask what it involves and how it will be adapted to your circumstances. An activity should not become a tool to pressure or police the other person.

questions.question: Is a repair the same as an apology?
paragraphs: Not always. A repair can be an attempt to interrupt escalation or restart a conversation. An apology can acknowledge responsibility. Neither replaces the behavior change or accountability that a particular hurt may require.

questions.question: How is this different from EFT?
paragraphs: Gottman-informed work organizes attention around friendship, conflict, meaning, trust, and commitment. [Emotionally Focused Therapy](/emotionally-focused-therapy-eft/) emphasizes attachment and emotional interactions. Clinicians may integrate ideas, but a coherent plan is more important than combining labels.

questions.question: Are the listed clinicians certified Gottman therapists?
paragraphs: This page does not make that claim. It links only to profiles naming Gottman-informed work or the approach. Certification and current availability require separate confirmation.

questions.question: What about private pay?
paragraphs: Couples consultations and couples sessions at M.F.T. are private pay. Request the fee and intended appointment type before booking; an approach name does not determine insurance coverage.
